---
title: "Bubble plot — Eukaryotic classes by coral type × health state (faceted)"
author: "Joana Krause"
date: "2026-08-11"
output: html_document
---

Faceted bubble plot of mean relative abundance (± SD) of eukaryotic classes across
coral types (complexa, robusta, black coral, octocoral) and health states (Diseased,
Healthy, Bleached). A union threshold keeps taxa consistent across facets. Three
concentric layers encode variability: outer halo = mean + SD, middle ring = mean,
inner core = mean − SD.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Load libraries

```{r load-libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)   # load dplyr AFTER plyr to avoid summarise/rename conflicts
library(rlang)   # sym(), %||%
```

# Load phyloseq object

```{r load-ps}
ps_plas_V3_V4 <- readRDS("../data/ps_final.rds")
```

# Faceted bubble plot — Eukaryotic classes by coral type × health state

```{r bubble-combined}
## =============================================================================
## PURPOSE:
##   Visualises the mean relative abundance of eukaryotic classes across coral
##   types (complexa, robusta, black coral, octocoral), faceted by coral health
##   condition (Healthy, Diseased, Bleached). Each bubble represents one
##   taxon × coral-type combination. Three concentric layers encode variability:
##     - Outermost halo  → mean + SD  (faint, shows upper spread)
##     - Middle ring     → mean       (semi-transparent)
##     - Inner core      → mean - SD  (solid, shows lower spread)
##
## INPUT:
##   A phyloseq object (ps_plas_V3_V4) containing an OTU/ASV table, taxonomy
##   table, and sample metadata. The metadata must include:
##     - "coral_health"     : values "healthy", "disease", "bleached"
##     - "complexa_robusta" : coral type used as the x-axis grouping
##   The taxonomy table must include "Class" and a higher-level "Subdivision"
##   column used for colouring.
##
## OUTPUT:
##   A faceted ggplot2 bubble plot saved as a PDF.
##
## DEPENDENCIES: phyloseq, dplyr, ggplot2, rlang
## =============================================================================

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 1) USER PARAMETERS — edit this section to adapt the script to your dataset
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## -- Core inputs --------------------------------------------------------------
ps_obj         <- ps_plas_V3_V4
health_var     <- "coral_health"
group_var      <- "complexa_robusta"
tax_rank       <- "Class"
mean_threshold <- 0.1

## -- Output -------------------------------------------------------------------
output_pdf <- "../output/bub/combined_class_mean_union_12aug.pdf"

## -- Axis ordering ------------------------------------------------------------
sample_order    <- c("complexa", "robusta", "black coral", "octocoral")
condition_order <- c("Diseased", "Healthy", "Bleached")

condition_labels <- c(
  "healthy"  = "Healthy",
  "disease"  = "Diseased",
  "bleached" = "Bleached"
)

class_sorted <- c(
  "Below Threshold",
  "Eukaryota_XXXX",
  "Archaeplastida_XXX",
  # Chlorophyta_X
  "Ulvophyceae", "Trebouxiophyceae", "Prasino-Clade-9", "Pyramimonadophyceae",
  "Pedinophyceae", "Chloropicophyceae", "Chlorophyta_XX", "Chlorophyceae", "Chlorodendrophyceae",
  # Prasinodermophyta_X
  "Prasinodermophyceae", "Palmophyllophyceae",
  # Rhodophyta_X
  "Rhodophyta_XX", "Stylonematophyceae", "Florideophyceae", "Compsopogonophyceae", "Bangiophyceae",
  # Cryptophyta_X
  "Cryptophyceae",
  # Haptophyta_X
  "Prymnesiophyceae", "Pavlovophyceae",
  # Rhizaria - Cercozoa
  "Chlorarachniophyceae",
  # Alveolata - Apicomplexa
  "Coccidiomorphea",
  # Alveolata - Chrompodellids
  "Colpodellidea",
  # Alveolata - Dinoflagellata
  "Dinophyceae",
  # Stramenopiles - Gyrista
  "Pinguiophyceae", "Phaeophyceae", "Pelagophyceae", "Mediophyceae",
  "Gyrista_X", "Eustigmatophyceae", "Dictyochophyceae",
  "Diatomeae_X", "Coscinodiscophyceae", "Chrysophyceae", "Bacillariophyceae"
)

## -- Subdivision colours ------------------------------------------------------
subdivision_order <- c(
  "Gyrista",
  "Chrompodellids", "Apicomplexa",
  "Haptophyta_X",
  "Cryptophyta_X",
  "Rhodophyta_X", "Prasinodermophyta_X", "Chlorophyta_X",
  "Archaeplastida_XX",
  "Eukaryota_XXX",
  "Below Threshold"
)

palette <- c(
  "Gyrista"             = "#9C85C0",
  "Apicomplexa"         = "#E69F00",
  "Chrompodellids"      = "#4DAF4A",
  "Haptophyta_X"        = "#674C2A",
  "Cryptophyta_X"       = "#DDCC77",
  "Rhodophyta_X"        = "#BD0A36",
  "Prasinodermophyta_X" = "#377EB8",
  "Chlorophyta_X"       = "#ABC817",
  "Archaeplastida_XX"   = "purple4",
  "Eukaryota_XXX"       = "#00bfffff",
  "Below Threshold"     = "#999999"
)

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 2) Helper function: process one health condition
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
## Wrapping the pipeline in a function avoids repeating it three times.
## All variable names that the function needs are explicit parameters
## (health_var, group_var, tax_rank) rather than free variables read from the
## global environment — this makes the function safe to reuse in other contexts.
##
## prune_samples() added to drop zero-sum samples before normalising;
## avoids 0/0 → NaN in transform_sample_counts().
## rename() uses !!sym(group_var) — the correct tidy-eval idiom.

process_condition <- function(ps, condition_value, display_label,
                              hvar, gvar, trank) {
  keep   <- sample_data(ps)[[hvar]] == condition_value
  ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)

  ps_sub %>%
    tax_glom(taxrank = trank) %>%
    prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 0, .) %>%          # zero-sum sample guard
    transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x) * 100) %>%
    psmelt() %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group = !!sym(gvar)) %>%            # correct tidy-eval rename
    group_by(
      OTU, Group,
      across(all_of(trank)),
      Subdivision
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      Abund_mean = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD         = sd(Abundance,   na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      SD        = replace(SD, is.na(SD), 0),
      Condition = display_label
    )
}

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 3) Process each condition and combine
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

dat_healthy  <- process_condition(ps_obj, "healthy",  "Healthy",  health_var, group_var, tax_rank)
dat_diseased <- process_condition(ps_obj, "disease",  "Diseased", health_var, group_var, tax_rank)
dat_bleached <- process_condition(ps_obj, "bleached", "Bleached", health_var, group_var, tax_rank)

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 4) Apply abundance threshold, re-aggregate, set factor levels, SD bounds
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
## THRESHOLD APPROACH — UNION:
##   A taxon is shown in ALL facets if its mean exceeds the threshold in ANY
##   one condition. This keeps the same y-axis taxa across facets for direct
##   visual comparison. The trade-off is that a taxon may appear with near-zero
##   abundance in a facet where it does not individually pass the threshold.
##
## Re-aggregation after collapsing prevents multiple overlapping bubbles for
## the same Group × Condition × "Below Threshold" combination.
## SD is pooled in quadrature (assumes independence between taxa).

dat_combined <- bind_rows(dat_healthy, dat_diseased, dat_bleached) %>%

  ## Mean per taxon within each condition (used for threshold test only)
  group_by(.data[[tax_rank]], Condition) %>%
  mutate(mean_abund_condition = mean(Abund_mean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  ## Union threshold: keep taxon if it passes in ANY condition
  group_by(.data[[tax_rank]]) %>%
  mutate(passes = any(mean_abund_condition > mean_threshold)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  ## Collapse taxa that don't pass
  mutate(
    !!tax_rank := if_else(passes, .data[[tax_rank]], "Below Threshold"),
    Subdivision = if_else(passes, Subdivision, "Below Threshold")
  ) %>%
  select(-mean_abund_condition, -passes) %>%

  ## Re-aggregate so every Group × Condition × "Below Threshold" row is one summed entry
  group_by(Group, Condition, .data[[tax_rank]], Subdivision) %>%
  summarise(
    Abund_mean = sum(Abund_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD         = sqrt(sum(SD^2,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%

  ## Ordered factors for axes and legend
  mutate(
    Condition    = factor(Condition,   levels = condition_order),
    Group        = factor(Group,       levels = sample_order),
    Subdivision  = factor(Subdivision, levels = subdivision_order),
    tax_rank_fct = factor(.data[[tax_rank]], levels = class_sorted)
  ) %>%

  ## SD halo bounds, clamped above zero
  mutate(
    Abund_upper = pmax(Abund_mean + SD, 1e-6),
    Abund_lower = pmax(Abund_mean - SD, 1e-6)
  )

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 5) Build the faceted bubble plot
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
##
## Three geom_point layers, drawn largest-to-smallest so inner layers are
## always visible on top:
##   Layer 1 (α = 0.20): Abund_upper — faint outer glow (mean + SD)
##   Layer 2 (α = 0.60): Abund_mean  — semi-transparent ring (mean)
##   Layer 3 (α = 1.00): Abund_lower — solid core (mean − SD)

bubp <- ggplot(
  dat_combined %>% filter(Abund_mean > 0),
  aes(x = Group, y = tax_rank_fct)
) +
  geom_point(   # outermost halo: mean + SD
    aes(size = Abund_upper, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 0.20, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(   # middle ring: mean
    aes(size = Abund_mean, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 0.60, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(   # inner solid core: mean − SD
    aes(size = Abund_lower, fill = Subdivision, color = Subdivision),
    alpha = 1.00, shape = 21, stroke = 0
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    limits = c(1e-6, 100),
    range  = c(0.1, 10),
    breaks = c(1, 10, 50, 75),
    guide  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(stroke = 0.5, alpha = 1, fill = "white"))
  ) +
  ## drop = TRUE: legend shows only subdivisions present in the data
  scale_fill_manual(values  = palette, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette, drop = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x    = "Coral Type",
    y    = "Eukaryotic Class",
    size = "Relative Abundance (%)",
    fill = "Eukaryotic Subdivision"
  ) +
  ggtitle("Microeukaryotic Classes in Coral Types") +
  facet_grid(. ~ Condition, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "lines"),
    plot.margin     = margin(5, 5, 5, 5),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(
    color = "none",
    fill  = guide_legend(
      title        = "Eukaryotic Subdivision",
      override.aes = list(size = 3, stroke = 0)
    )
  )

print(bubp)

## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 6) Save to PDF
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

dir.create("../output/bub", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave(
  filename = output_pdf,
  plot     = bubp,
  width    = 7,
  height   = 8,
  dpi      = 300
)
```
